_note: Kanto as HeartGold and SoulSilver show it (A-66: Zack, “HeartGold does both of them”), the same way biology/johto.json holds Johto, and read together with it. Every Kanto place in the games is a node; Route 26, 27 and 28, Tohjo Falls, Victory Road and Mt. Silver are in johto.json, where they were first. The connections are the games' own map (class mechanic), from the HeartGold decomp (pret/pokeheartgold 6988158): where two places' map blocks meet on the overworld matrix or a warp leads from one to the other, with the Magnet Train (Goldenrod to Saffron) and the S.S. Aqua (Olivine to Vermilion) as the two crossings by rail and sea. Route 3 and Route 4 meet on the matrix but Mt. Moon stands between them, so they are joined only through it. Region is the map header's own (Kanto or Johto). Biome, elevation and water are Blackthorn's reading of each place, from the Pokégear's own description of it (quoted in its note), how it looks in the games and how its Pokémon are found (class inferred), as Johto's are; edit them freely. xy places it on the drawing: the Pokégear map's coordinates, scaled to match the Johto drawing, nudged where two places share a square.

kanto-route-22.name: Route 22
kanto-route-22.note: the Pokégear: “A path to Victory Road that eventually becomes impassable.” Grass and a pond west of Viridian

indigo-plateau.name: Indigo Plateau
indigo-plateau.note: the Pokégear: “The fate of many Trainers aiming for the top rests here.” The Pokémon League, above Victory Road

viridian-city.name: Viridian City
viridian-city.note: the Pokégear: “A beautiful city that is enveloped in green year-round.” A pond at its edge

kanto-route-1.name: Route 1
kanto-route-1.note: the Pokégear: “A country road full of greenery and rough paths.”

pallet-town.name: Pallet Town
pallet-town.note: the Pokégear: “A fairly new and quiet town. It’s a small and pretty place.” The sea is to its south

kanto-route-2.name: Route 2
kanto-route-2.note: the Pokégear: “A path that winds and bends from the forest’s entrance.” Two parts, west and east of Viridian Forest

viridian-forest.name: Viridian Forest
viridian-forest.note: the Pokégear: “A forest filled with nature and Bug-type Pokémon.” A closed forest between Viridian and Pewter

pewter-city.name: Pewter City
pewter-city.note: the Pokégear: “A quiet city nestled between rugged mountains and rocks.”

kanto-route-3.name: Route 3
kanto-route-3.note: the Pokégear: “A road where many rocks have fallen from the sky to create craters.”

mt-moon.name: Mt. Moon
mt-moon.note: the Pokégear: “A mountain where a star fell. It now holds a mysterious power.” A cave through the mountain, with Mt. Moon Square open to the sky on top

kanto-route-4.name: Route 4
kanto-route-4.note: the Pokégear: “A one-way road down a hill that has a gentle slope and is fun to traverse.” A pond below the hill

cerulean-city.name: Cerulean City
cerulean-city.note: the Pokégear: “A beautiful city with flowing water and blooming flowers.”

cerulean-cave.name: Cerulean Cave
cerulean-cave.note: the Pokégear: “A cave that had collapsed once. It has been reconstructed.” Deep water inside

kanto-route-24.name: Route 24
kanto-route-24.note: the Pokégear: “A beautiful bridge that stretches across a river.”

kanto-route-25.name: Route 25
kanto-route-25.note: the Pokégear: “A path that winds through the forest and comes out overlooking the sea.” Bill’s Sea Cottage is at its end

kanto-route-5.name: Route 5
kanto-route-5.note: the Pokégear: “A road running north of Saffron City connecting to the Underground Path.”

kanto-route-6.name: Route 6
kanto-route-6.note: the Pokégear: “A road running south of Saffron City connecting to the Underground Path.” A pond by the road

saffron-city.name: Saffron City
saffron-city.note: the Pokégear: “The biggest city in Kanto, shining with a golden light.” The Magnet Train runs from here to Goldenrod

kanto-route-7.name: Route 7
kanto-route-7.note: the Pokégear: “A short road that leads to the blocked-off Underground Path.” Between Celadon and Saffron

kanto-route-8.name: Route 8
kanto-route-8.note: the Pokégear: “A short road that leads to the blocked-off Underground Path.” Between Saffron and Lavender

celadon-city.name: Celadon City
celadon-city.note: the Pokégear: “A rich, rainbow-colored city where people and Pokémon gather.” Its pond holds Grimer and Muk

kanto-route-9.name: Route 9
kanto-route-9.note: the Pokégear: “A road that forms a maze crossing a small, rocky mountain.”

kanto-route-10.name: Route 10
kanto-route-10.note: the Pokégear: “A road that passes along the canal and comes out at the Power Plant.” North and south parts, either side of Rock Tunnel

rock-tunnel.name: Rock Tunnel
rock-tunnel.note: the Pokégear: “A dark tunnel that begins in Lavender Town and comes out in Cerulean City.” It needs Flash

kanto-power-plant.name: Power Plant
kanto-power-plant.note: the Pokégear: “The plant that generates all the energy for the Kanto region.” A building on the canal; no wild Pokémon in HeartGold or SoulSilver

lavender-town.name: Lavender Town
lavender-town.note: the Pokégear: “A small town covered in a beautiful hue of purple.” The Radio Tower and the House of Memories; no wild Pokémon

vermilion-city.name: Vermilion City
vermilion-city.note: the Pokégear: “A southern city that is bathed in orange by the setting sun.” A port: the S.S. Aqua sails from here to Olivine

digletts-cave.name: Diglett's Cave
digletts-cave.note: the Pokégear: “A tunnel dug by DIGLETT connecting Vermilion City to Pewter City.” It runs from Route 2 to Route 11

kanto-route-11.name: Route 11
kanto-route-11.note: the Pokégear: “A grassy path with a gentle, refreshing breeze.”

kanto-route-12.name: Route 12
kanto-route-12.note: the Pokégear: “A bridge known for its fishing. It’s also called “Silence Bridge.””

kanto-route-13.name: Route 13
kanto-route-13.note: the Pokégear: “A difficult, narrow path where many Trainers await you.”

kanto-route-14.name: Route 14
kanto-route-14.note: the Pokégear: “A pleasant coastal road where the breeze blows and waves roar.”

kanto-route-15.name: Route 15
kanto-route-15.note: the Pokégear: “A path that cuts through the row of trees to come out on the coastline.”

kanto-route-16.name: Route 16
kanto-route-16.note: the Pokégear: “The northern starting point of Cycling Road.”

kanto-route-17.name: Route 17
kanto-route-17.note: the Pokégear: “An easy path of Cycling Road running above the sea.”

kanto-route-18.name: Route 18
kanto-route-18.note: the Pokégear: “The southern ending point of Cycling Road.”

fuchsia-city.name: Fuchsia City
fuchsia-city.note: the Pokégear: “A historic village that has become new.” Ponds in the town

pal-park.name: Pal Park
pal-park.note: the Pokégear: “This used to be the location of the Safari Zone, but is now the Pal Park.” Pokémon brought from the Game Boy Advance games are caught here; no wild community

kanto-sea-route-19.name: Sea Route 19
kanto-sea-route-19.note: the Pokégear: “A coastal road littered with rocks due to Cinnabar Island’s volcano eruption.”

kanto-sea-route-20.name: Sea Route 20
kanto-sea-route-20.note: the Pokégear: “A popular path with swimmers. The Seafoam Islands are also here.”

seafoam-islands.name: Seafoam Islands
seafoam-islands.note: the Pokégear: “Two small islands lightly floating in the ocean.” A cave of five floors; Blaine’s Gym moved into it after the eruption

cinnabar-island.name: Cinnabar Island
cinnabar-island.note: the Pokégear: “A town used to be here until it was swept away by an eruption.” Only the Pokémon Center is left, and the mouth of the volcano is still open

kanto-sea-route-21.name: Sea Route 21
kanto-sea-route-21.note: the Pokégear: “A coastal road where the only threat might be the volcano on the horizon.” Patches of grass among the water

viridian-forest.name: Viridian Forest
viridian-forest.why: Kanto's forest: a closed wood between Viridian and Pewter that the Pokégear calls “filled with nature and Bug-type Pokémon”, with both bug lines, the forest's birds and its Pikachu

mt-moon.name: Mt. Moon
mt-moon.why: a mountain cave the games say a star fell on, with a pond in Mt. Moon Square on top: Zubat, Geodude, Paras, Sandshrew and the Clefairy, an energy-poor system fed from outside

seafoam-islands.name: Seafoam Islands
seafoam-islands.why: a sea cave: Seel and Dewgong, Horsea, Krabby, Slowbro and Jynx in the dark, the sea's life washing in, and the Zubat that roost above the water

cerulean-cave.name: Cerulean Cave
cerulean-cave.why: the deepest cave in Kanto, reopened after the games say it collapsed: a lake in the dark and a community of evolved Pokémon, Ditto among them

fuchsia-routes.name: The routes around Fuchsia
fuchsia-routes.why: the south-east side where the Safari Zone used to be: Silence Bridge, the coast roads and the tree-lined Route 15, with the Nidoran lines, Tangela, Hoppip and the rare Chansey

cinnabar-seas.name: Cinnabar and its seas
cinnabar-seas.why: the volcanic island and the open sea around it: the games say the eruption swept the town away and the volcano's mouth is still open; Tentacool, Shellder, Chinchou, Staryu and Corsola in the water
